newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn denies Germany pushing single EU tax plans.
newsitem.headline: Bonn denies Germany pushing single EU tax plans.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry on Thursday denied a British newspaper report that France and Germany were leading a quiet effort to create a single European tax system.

"There are no such plans by the German government," a ministry spokesman told Reuters. "The finance and tax policies remain in the hands of member states, even after introduction of economic and monetary union."

The Independent newspaper reported on Thursday that an alliance of countries including France and Germany were preparing plans for a single tax system. It said the proposals envisaged control over income tax being pooled by national governments inside the area covered by the planned single European currency.
A spokesman at the office of British Prime Minister John Major said Britain was not aware of talks along these lines.
The French Finance Ministry also denied the report.
The German finance ministry spokesman, referring to the so-called stability pact agreed at the EU summit in Dublin to penalise profligate borrowing after European monetary union (EMU), said:
"The stability pact...offers the necessary instruments for congruent finance policies."
